Purpose statement 
This technical brief describes a prototype Oracle APEX application that 
enables natural language query of Oracle E-Business Suite data by leveraging 
Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI). 
This application utilizes advanced generative AI technology to provide content 
and insights. While we strive for accuracy and reliability in the output 
generated, k

now that AI-driven solutions are not always accurate and 
occasionally produce unexpected results.  
Users should exercise their own judgment when interpreting the application's 
output and verify any generated content before making decisions or taking 
actions based on it. The use of this application is at your own discretion, and 
Oracle Corporation and its affiliates disclaim any liability for any damages 
caused by use of this software. 
This application is a prototype provided for demonstration purposes. It is not 
intended as a reference implementation to be cloned or customized. 
The application is currently available only in English and does not support 
user preferences such as time zone or date or number formats.

Functional Overview 
This technical brief demonstrates how to enable natural language to SQL query translation for Oracle E-Business 
Suite data. 
The following screenshots show how a user can ask the sys

tem questions in English, and the system responds by 
displaying records that directly answer these questions.  
 
Manufacturing Example. In the Ask Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) page, a user entered the prompt show the details of the work orders released in the last 2 
weeks which are delayed. The system responded with a list of work orders released in the last two weeks and are delayed, listed by Job Name. 
 
HCM Example 1. In the Ask Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) page, a user entered the prompt Show employees with more than 25 years of experience along 
with their qualifications. The system responded with a list of employee names together with their years of experience and qualification.

Clearing Conversation Context 
Notice that most of the questions are conversational, enabling the next question to refer to the preceding 
question using anaphoric references. By default, OCI Generative AI assumes you are asking a follow-up question.  
To clear the context and start a new line of questioning, click New Conversation. 
 
Selecting a Domain 
If you know the business domain of your question, you can select it from the Domain drop-down list. This 
provides a hint to the generative AI and may produce a more accurate answer to your question.

For diagnostic purposes, it is useful to view the SQL statement generated by the OCI Generative AI

service. The 
administrator may enable a Show SQL button for a particular user. This button is disabled by default but can be 
turned on by a user-level profile option FND: NLQ Show SQL. 
 
To enable this button for a user: 
1. Log in to E-Business Suite as SYSADMIN. 
2. Navigate to Functional Administrator.  
3. Click Core Services then click Profiles. 
4. In the Code field, enter FND_NLQ_SHOW_SQL then click Go. 
5. Click Update Value. 
6. Click the User tab. 
7. Click Add. 
8. In the User field, enter the user for whom to enable this feature. 
9. In the Value field, enter Yes. 
10. Click Update.

Technical Overview 
The following architecture diagram shows the interaction between the technical components used. 
 
This Architecture Diagram shows the interaction between the APEX Frontend, ADB on OCI, the LLM Service,

and EBS. 
1. APEX Frontend 
This implementation uses Oracle APEX to develop the user interface and integrate with Oracle E-Business Suite 
(EBS) Single Sign-On (SSO) for user authentication. The APEX app is embedded within OA Framework and 
ensures that the EBS security setup is honored. In addition to SSO, standard EBS FND_USER authentication is also 
supported. 
 
The APEX UI sends the natural language question to the Oracle Autonomous Database (ADB) using its Select AI 
API (DBMS_CLOUD_API) package. The ADB returns a SQL query that addresses the question. 
2. Oracle Autonomous Database 
Upon receipt of a natural language question, the ADB’s Select AI feature generates an appropriate prompt and 
sends it to the Oracle Generative AI service. 
 
The ADB is configured with several AI profiles. You can think of an AI profile as a domain expert that answers 
questions for a particular business domain. Technically, an AI profile is an ADB object that contains a subset of 
EBS metadata (ess

entially, view names) that can best solve the questions in its domain.  
 
For example, the sample software (Refer to Downloading the Sample Software) contains the following AI profiles 
to answer questions for a corresponding business domain: 
 
AI PROFILE NAME 
BUSINESS DOMAIN 
EBS_NLQ_DMFCST_PROFILE 
Discrete Costing 
EBS_NLQ_DMF_PROFILE 
Discrete Manufacturing 
EBS_NLQ_AR_PROFILE 
Dispute 
EBS_NLQ_INV_PROFILE 
Logistics

Given a natural language question, the sample code’s logic chooses the most relevant AI profile that has the 
highest probability of answering the question correctly. It then instruct

s the ADB to use this profile to compose a 
prompt. The SQL statement returned by the generative AI service’s Large Language Model (LLM) contains views 
and columns constrained by this AI profile. The AI profile concept provides a way to constrain the number of 
database objects that the LLM must analyze, resulting in better performance and accuracy. 
 
Notice that the ADB does not contain any data, only schema metadata (such as view definitions), so your data is 
never exposed to any third-party systems. 
3. Generative AI Large Language Model 
Ultimately, the OCI Generative AI LLM is responsible for constructing a valid SQL query.  
4. E-Business Suite Database 
The code provided checks the syntax of the SQL response received from the LLM by way of the Autonomous 
Database Select AI API return value. If the SQL response is valid, APEX forwards the response to the EBS database 
for execution. A table displays the records returned by the SQL response. The SQL executes in a new custom 
s

chema with the minimally required READ privileges to provide maximum security. Virtual Private Databases 
(VPDs) guarantee that the end user has the authority to view the returned records. See the Security Overview for a 
more detailed explanation.

Security Overview 
The following software security best practices have been considered during the integration of Oracle E-Business 
Suite (EBS) with an OCI Generative AI service provider:  
• 
Separation of Duties 
• 
Principle of Least Privilege 
• 
Single Sign-On Authentication 
• 
Role-Based Access Control 
• 
Record-Level Data Security 
• 
Privacy by Design  
• 
Audit Logging 
Separation of Duties 
Separation of Duties addresses the concern of exposing your data to a third-party AI service provider by 
separating tasks into two distinct duties: 
1. Converting a natu

ral language question into a valid SQL query. 
2. Executing the SQL query to retrieve the results. 
As shown in the previous Architecture Diagram, the above two duties are achieved by two distinct code paths. The 
top half of the diagram is responsible for constructing the SQL. In this pathway, the AI service provider is 
contacted by the Oracle Autonomous Database, but there is no customer data exchanged, only EBS metadata 
(view definitions). When the returned SQL query is executed as illustrated in the bottom half of the diagram, the 
AI service provider is no longer involved. This facilitates the separation of duties principle. 
Principle of Least Privilege 
To prevent the SQL from querying all data and from using  SQL commands such as INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or 
DROP TABLE, a new schema (named XX_NLQ) is created in your database. This new schema has minimal 
privileges, as illustrated in the following diagram:  
 
XX_NLQ Schema: The new XX_NLQ Schema in EBS is defined with minimal

privileges. 
Single Sign-On Authentication 
 
11 Enabling Natural Language Query of Oracle E-Business Suite Release 12.2, Leveraging OCI Generative AI 
 
  
 
Copyright © 2024, Oracle and/or its affiliates 
 
 
This implementation uses Oracle E-Business Suite's authentication setup to authenticate the user. This is 
achieved by a new OA Framework enhancement. For more information about this enhancement, refer to this 
Oracle technical brief:  Extending Oracle E-Business Suite Release 12.2 Using Oracle APEX  
Role-Based Access Control 
This implementation uses Oracle E-Business Suite’s comprehensive Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) security 
feature to grant a user access to an AI profile. You can grant access either explicitly or indirectly, by granting AI 
profile access to a Responsibility. See Configuring Security. 
For more information about the general EBS RBAC feature, see Oracle Support Document 1537100.1, Function 
Security and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) in Oracle E-Busi

ness Suite. 
Record-Level Data Security 
This implementation provides fine-grain record-level security. Each data source is a view with an accompanying 
PL/SQL security handler. By creating a Virtual Private Database (VPD) policy on the data source and then 
performing a SELECT command, the database engine calls the PL/SQL security handler, which returns a WHERE 
clause that filters out all unauthorized records from the view. Because VPD is an underlying database technology, 
there is no complex, manually-coded security logic to introduce security vulnerabilities. 
Privacy by Design 
Oracle Development curates the data sources and takes care during the design phase to ensure that columns 
containing critical data, such as HIPAA and PCI information, are excluded from the views. This eliminates the risk 
of accidentally exposing such data. Even if the LLM constructs a query to select from those columns, the query 
fails since no such columns exist in the curated views. The secured views

only select the minimally required 
columns from the base views. Since the query is performed in the XX_NLQ Schema, there is no possibility of 
extracting critical data from the database. 
Audit Logging 
The implementation logs every question and the results (SQLs) in a logging table. This logging table serves the 
following two purposes: 
• 
The data can be used for debugging and improving accuracy. 
• 
A DBA can review the data to determine if there are any malicious attempts or misuse of the solution.  
The table is available in the Autonomous Database schema XX_NLQ_UTIL. The table name is 
FND_NLQ_SESSION_HISTORY.

Subscribing to OCI Generative AI 
This implementation uses Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI to perform natural language to SQL 
translation.  
1. Subscribe to OCI Generative AI. 
To use

OCI Generative AI, subscribe to an OCI region that offers OCI Generative AI. Refer to Subscribing to an 
Infrastructure Region for more information and instructions. 
Not all OCI regions support Generative AI. Refer to Regions with Generative AI for more information. 
2. Note the OCI Generative AI API Endpoint Information. 
During the installation, you will be prompted to enter your OCI Generative AI API information. Note the 
following information: 
1. Refer to the Generative AI Service Inference API page and note the API Endpoint of your subscribed 
region. This will be referred to as the ocigenai_endpoint in a subsequent step. Currently, it can be 
one of the following URLs: 
 
From the OCI Generative AI Chat API page, note the POST API name. This will be referred to as 
ocigenai_chat_api in a subsequent step. Currently, it is shown as /20231130/actions/chat: 
 
Important: The leading forward slash is part of the API signature. Do not omit the leading forward slash. 
3. (Highly Rec

ommended) Create a Service Gateway. 
The OCI Generative AI REST endpoint resides in the public internet. If you do not want any network traffic 
exposed to the public internet, create a Service Gateway in your OCI Virtual Cloud Network (VCN). See Access 
to Oracle Services: Service Gateway for more information and instructions.  
Additionally, when you create the Oracle Autonomous Database instance, you must create it in the same VCN 
and region as the OCI Generative AI. This ensures that the traffic from the VCN to the OCI Generative AI 
service travels over the Oracle network instead of the internet.

Troubleshooting 
Test with Select AI’s Chat Mode 
If the application does not produce any results, perform a standalone test using the standard Select AI chat mode. 
This verifies the OCI Resource Principal authentication configuration has been correctly configured. 
Connect to the Autonomous Database as the XX_NLQ_UTIL user.  Run the following SQL statements: 
-- Create a test AI Profile  
BEGIN

DBMS_CLOUD_AI.CREATE_PROFILE(                                               
      profile_name => 'TESTGENAI',                                                  
      attributes => '{"provider": "oci",                       
                     "credential_name": "OCI$RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL", 
                     "object_list": [{"owner": "XX_NLQ_UTIL", "name": "DUAL"}], 
                     "model": "meta.llama-3.1-70b-instruct", 
                     "temperature":"0.4", 
                     "oci_apiformat": "GENERIC"                               
                    }' 
    );                                                          
END;  
/ 
Since an LLM model may be deprecated and replaced by a more advanced version, refer to the Chat Models 
section in the Pretrained Foundational Models in Generative AI OCI documentation topic. If the meta.llama-
3.1-70b-instruct model is no longer available, replace the “model” value above with the current version. 
-- Try the stan

dard Select AI chat mode 
SELECT DBMS_CLOUD_AI.GENERATE(prompt        => 'What is Oracle DB', 
                              profile_name  => 'TESTGENAI', 
                              action        => 'chat') 
FROM DUAL;

not been activated yet. Due to caching, it may take up to two hours for your changes to take effect.

Conclusion 
Oracle E-Business Suite provides many powerful querying and reporting features. But most of these querying 
features are very sophisticated and require in-depth user training to use them effectively. This paper presents a 
natural language query system for Oracle E-Business Suite. The system leverages Oracle Autonomous Database’s 
Select AI feature and OCI Generative AI which translates an English question into a SQL query. The SQL query is 
then executed in the EBS database to provide the results. Each query is executed in a new XX_NLQ schema that 
has minimum grants. Together with new secured views and new VPD policies, the Oracle E-Business Suite 
security setup is honored. The system utilizes Oracle APEX to provide a simple and intuitive Ask Oracle E-Bus

iness 
Suite user interface.
